A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same study, Is In-Context Learning Learning? Text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-E support reliable comparison; all appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with four LLMs across nine synthetic tasks, including accuracy comparisons, distribution-shift evaluations and ablations in Sections 5-6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results and ablations in Sections 5-6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The prompting procedures, model usage and inference configurations in Section 4 and Appendices C/E are unchanged. The theoretical correction does not introduce or modify a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine synthetic tasks and the same distribution-shift scenarios, covering formal-language recognition, graph/maze tasks and vending-machine arithmetic.

E2.justification: The evaluated LLMs and prompting strategies are unchanged. Decision-tree, kNN and MLP baselines retain the same participation in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same sample sizes, distribution shifts, shot counts, model configurations and evaluation procedures. Equation 1 corrects the theoretical error definition; the PDFs do not report a changed experimental metric or scoring procedure.

E4.justification: The lexical corruption, exemplar ordering, altered-distribution and compliance-versus-learning analyses in Section 6 and Appendix D are unchanged. The new bias-variance explanation adds discussion, not an analysis.

E5.justification: Standard-deviation reporting and baseline seed information are unchanged. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and result plots, including those in Appendix D, are identical. Reported accuracies, slopes, rankings and empirical findings are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes the indicator from f(x)=c(x) to f(x)!=c(x), correcting the error definition. Section 3.3 also qualifies the claim that the prompt contribution vanishes by adding 'when equiprobable to the exemplars.' Appendix A and the remaining mathematical development are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims that ICL constitutes learning but has limited, distribution-sensitive generalisation. The added emergent-capabilities remark frames these existing claims without changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly suggests the bias-variance tradeoff as a possible explanation for lower accuracy with fully randomised exemplars. Section 3 also softens its description of what existing formalisms overlook. The stated limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Model versions, hardware, token limits, temperature, APO settings, baseline preprocessing, sample prompts and code-access information are unchanged in Section 10 and Appendices C/E.

R1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit connection between limited cross-task generalisation and disagreement with some emergent-capability claims. This is a small positioning addition; Section 2 and the cited works are unchanged.

P1.justification: A few sentences in the introduction, theoretical background and discussion are revised, while section order and overall narrative remain intact. The Section 3 rewrite introduces the duplicated word 'noting.'

P2.justification: Local equation and paragraph reflow changes spacing and page breaks around pages 3-4 and 10-12. All figures and tables retain their design, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Equation 1 to count errors rather than correct predictions and qualifies the prompt-contribution argument in Section 3.3. These provide a limited improvement in mathematical accuracy and scope. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the added bias-variance interpretation remains tentative.
